title: Boss: the first week on the job
summary: Read a messy working tree, split it into clean commits, and build the tools that model it.

steps.title: The scene
body: It is your first week. You cloned the team's repo, fixed a bug, started a feature, and ran a build. Now `git status -s` is a wall of letters and your lead wants **two clean commits**: the bug fix alone, then the feature.
Everything in this module comes together: the three areas, status codes, diffs, ignore rules and messages.

steps.prompt: Your fix is in `Cart.cs`; the feature touched `Cart.cs` too (a different hunk) and added `Coupon.cs`. `.gitignore` has `bin/`. What does `git status -s` print before you stage anything?
code: # on disk now: Cart.cs (2 changed hunks), Coupon.cs (new), bin/Shop.dll
steps.explain: `Cart.cs` is modified but unstaged. `Coupon.cs` is new. `bin/` is ignored, so the build output is not listed.

steps.prompt: Arrange the commands to produce the two commits: the fix first, then the feature.
lines: git commit -m "Fix rounding in cart total"
steps.explain: `git add -p` lets you stage only the fix hunk. Check it with `git diff --staged`, commit, then stage the rest (the feature hunk and the new file) for the second commit.

steps.title: Ignore rules
prompt: Write `Ignored(string path, List<string> patterns)` implementing this subset of `.gitignore` (paths use `/`, like `src/bin/app.dll`):
- `name/` (ends with `/`): ignored if any **folder** in the path is named `name` (not the file name itself).
- `*.ext`: ignored if the **file name** (last segment) ends with `.ext`.
- `name` (anything else): ignored if any segment, folder or file, equals `name`.
- Patterns are checked in order and the **last matching pattern wins**.
bin/app.dll -> true     logs/a.log -> true     logs/keep.log -> false
src/Program.cs -> false .env -> true           bin -> false (a file called bin)
starter: static bool Ignored(string path, List<string> patterns)
solution: static bool Ignored(string path, List<string> patterns)
hints: Split the path on `/`. Folders are every segment except the last.
Loop through all patterns and set `ignored = !negate` each time one matches.
For `!keep.log`, strip the `!` and then match `keep.log` like any other plain name.
template: Dojo.Eq("logs/keep.log is re-included", false, Ignored("logs/keep.log", dojoP));
Dojo.Eq("a file named bin is not a folder", false, Ignored("bin", dojoP));
Dojo.Eq("last match wins", true, Ignored("keep.log", new List<string> { "!keep.log", "*.log" }));

steps.title: Status that respects .gitignore
prompt: Combine the two models. Write `StatusWithIgnore(head, index, work, patterns)` that behaves like `ShortStatus` from lesson 1, except that **untracked** paths matching the ignore rules are left out. Tracked files are always reported, even if a pattern matches them (that is how real Git behaves).
Your code must include both `ShortStatus` and `Ignored` (rewrite or paste them).
starter: static List<string> StatusWithIgnore(Dictionary<string, string> head, Dictionary<string, string> index, Dictionary<string, string> work, List<string> patterns)
solution: static List<string> ShortStatus(Dictionary<string, string> head, Dictionary<string, string> index, Dictionary<string, string> work)
bool inHead = head.ContainsKey(p), inIndex = index.ContainsKey(p), inWork = work.ContainsKey(p);
static bool Ignored(string path, List<string> patterns)
static List<string> StatusWithIgnore(Dictionary<string, string> head, Dictionary<string, string> index, Dictionary<string, string> work, List<string> patterns)
hints: Only drop lines that start with `?? ` and whose path (`line[3..]`) is ignored.
template: Dojo.Eq("ignored untracked files are hidden, tracked ones still show", new List<string> { " M Cart.cs", " M app.log", "?? Coupon.cs" },
Dojo.Eq("no patterns behaves like ShortStatus", new List<string> { " M Cart.cs", " M app.log", "?? Coupon.cs", "?? bin/Shop.dll", "?? run.log" },

steps.title: Review gate
prompt: Before pushing, your team runs a script that checks each new commit's message. Write `Review(List<string> messages)` that returns one line per message: `OK: <subject>` if it passes the linter from lesson 4, otherwise `FAIL: <subject> (<problems joined with ", ">)`. Include your `Lint` method.
solution: if (subject.EndsWith(".")) problems.Add("subject ends with a period");
if (lines.Length > 1 && lines[1] != "") problems.Add("no blank line after subject");
if (lines.Skip(1).Any(l => l.Length > 72)) problems.Add("body line longer than 72");
template: Dojo.Eq("mixed batch", new List<string> { "OK: Add coupons", "FAIL: fix. (subject ends with a period)", "FAIL: Tidy (no blank line after subject)" },
